title: mTORC1: Two Signals at the Lysosome

scenes.visual: Dark navy background (#0B1020). A large cell cross-section fills 70% of frame height: slate-blue plasma membrane curving across the top, warm teal-bordered oval lysosome in the lower center, and faint gold protein blocks drifting gently in the cytoplasm. Title fades in cleanly across the upper center in bold white (size 44): 'mTORC1: Two Signals at the Lysosome', then dissolves out as the cell stays alive.

scenes.tts: Building new protein burns amino acids and a large share of cellular energy. So how does a cell decide it can afford to grow? Starting without permission or raw materials wastes scarce supplies. One central kinase complex, em-tor C one, makes that call.
scenes.caption: Building new protein burns amino acids and a large share of cellular energy. So how does a cell decide it can afford to grow? Starting without permission or raw materials wastes scarce supplies. One central kinase complex, mTORC1, makes that call.
scenes.visual: Same cell cross-section (colour map carried throughout both films: emerald #2ECC71 for growth-factor/Akt/Rheb, crimson #E05A47 for TSC brake, sky cyan #38BDF8 for amino acids/Rags, gold #F4B942 for mTORC1, teal border for lysosome). Schematic ribosomes pulse faintly on the right while an ATP bar ticks down slightly. A gold block labelled 'mTORC1' (size 30) drifts into focus in the cytoplasm.
scenes.narration: Building new protein burns amino acids and a large share of cellular energy. So how does a cell decide it can afford to grow? Starting without permission or raw materials wastes scarce supplies. One central kinase complex, mTORC1, makes that call.

scenes.tts: Before this kinase switches on, it checks two separate questions. First, has the body sent a growth factor saying it is time to grow? Second, are there enough amino acids on hand to build protein? Two independent tracks carry those two answers straight to the lysosome.
scenes.caption: Before this kinase switches on, it checks two separate questions. First, has the body sent a growth factor saying it is time to grow? Second, are there enough amino acids on hand to build protein? Two independent tracks carry those two answers straight to the lysosome.
scenes.visual: Same cell cross-section; two glowing lanes appear in place. On the left, an emerald lane runs from a plasma-membrane receptor down toward the lysosome rim, labelled 'Growth factor?' (size 28). On the right, a sky-cyan lane runs from drifting cyan amino acid dots to the lysosome rim, labelled 'Amino acids?' (size 28). Both lanes converge on the teal lysosome.
scenes.narration: Before this kinase switches on, it checks two separate questions. First, has the body sent a growth factor saying it is time to grow? Second, are there enough amino acids on hand to build protein? Two independent tracks carry those two answers straight to the lysosome.

scenes.tts: Follow the growth factor track first. A signal such as insulin activates the kinase AKT at the plasma membrane. On the lysosome sits a small switch protein called Rheb. The TSC complex holds it off by making Rheb cut its GTP to GDP. AKT phosphorylates TSC, lifting that brake right off Rheb.
scenes.caption: Follow the growth-factor track first. A signal such as insulin activates the kinase Akt at the plasma membrane. On the lysosome sits a small switch protein called Rheb. The TSC complex holds it off by making Rheb cut its GTP to GDP. Akt phosphorylates TSC, lifting that brake right off Rheb.
scenes.visual: Zoom slightly into the left-center of the same cell. An emerald growth-factor diamond binds the membrane receptor; an emerald 'Akt' block lights up and glides down. On the teal lysosome rim, a dim lipid-anchored block labelled 'Rheb' sits clamped under a crimson 'TSC' brake block. Akt stamps a bright yellow 'P' onto crimson TSC, which uncouples and drifts away. Empathy fix: Show 'TSC: Rheb-GTP → Rheb-GDP' beside the crimson brake as the mechanism is spoken.
scenes.narration: Follow the growth-factor track first. A signal such as insulin activates the kinase Akt at the plasma membrane. On the lysosome sits a small switch protein called Rheb. The TSC complex holds it off by making Rheb cut its GTP to GDP. Akt phosphorylates TSC, lifting that brake right off Rheb.

scenes.tts: With the TSC brake lifted, Rheb stays loaded with GTP. Active Rheb is the direct activator of em-tor C one. Notice where Rheb sits, though. A lipid tail anchors Rheb to internal membranes, including the lysosome. Meanwhile, the kinase complex still drifts out in the cytoplasm.
scenes.caption: With the TSC brake lifted, Rheb stays loaded with GTP. Active Rheb is the direct activator of mTORC1. Notice where Rheb sits, though. A lipid tail anchors Rheb to internal membranes, including the lysosome. Meanwhile, the kinase complex still drifts out in the cytoplasm.
scenes.visual: Crimson TSC fades back. The anchored Rheb block on the lysosome rim turns bright emerald green with a glowing 'GTP' tag (label 'Rheb-GTP', size 28), pulsing gently. Its wavy lipid tail is anchored in the lysosome membrane. Across a clear gap of dark cytoplasm, gold 'mTORC1' blocks remain unlit and drifting out of reach, visualizing spatial separation.
scenes.narration: With the TSC brake lifted, Rheb stays loaded with GTP. Active Rheb is the direct activator of mTORC1. Notice where Rheb sits, though. A lipid tail anchors Rheb to internal membranes, including the lysosome. Meanwhile, the kinase complex still drifts out in the cytoplasm.

scenes.tts: Now follow the amino acid track. Another pair of small switches, the Rag proteins, sit anchored on that same lysosome surface. The Rags do not activate the kinase directly. Instead, when amino acids rise, the Rags grab em-tor C one and pull it onto the lysosome.
scenes.caption: Now follow the amino acid track. Another pair of small switches, the Rag proteins, sit anchored on that same lysosome surface. The Rags do not activate the kinase directly. Instead, when amino acids rise, the Rags grab mTORC1 and pull it onto the lysosome.
scenes.visual: Same lysosome view. Sky-cyan amino acid dots stream into the cell around the lysosome (labelled 'Amino acids', size 28). A paired cyan block anchored on the lysosome rim, labelled 'Rags', flips into an active gripping shape. The Rags latch onto gold 'mTORC1' via its notched side tab (Raptor) and reel mTORC1 onto the lysosome right beside emerald Rheb-GTP.
scenes.narration: Now follow the amino acid track. Another pair of small switches, the Rag proteins, sit anchored on that same lysosome surface. The Rags do not activate the kinase directly. Instead, when amino acids rise, the Rags grab mTORC1 and pull it onto the lysosome.

scenes.tts: Separating activation from delivery builds a strict cellular gate. Test it yourself. Suppose amino acids are plentiful, so the Rags hold the complex right on the lysosome. Now remove the growth factor from outside the cell. Does the kinase switch on, or stay off?
scenes.caption: Separating activation from delivery builds a strict cellular gate. Test it yourself. Suppose amino acids are plentiful, so the Rags hold the complex right on the lysosome. Now remove the growth factor from outside the cell. Does the kinase switch on, or stay off?
scenes.visual: Same lysosome scene. Sky-cyan amino acids remain abundant and cyan Rags hold gold 'mTORC1' docked on the lysosome rim. At the top plasma membrane, the emerald growth factor vanishes and Akt dims. Clean top banner (size 30): 'Amino acids present, no growth factor: mTORC1 ON or OFF?'. TSC and Rheb pulse gently with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Separating activation from delivery builds a strict cellular gate. Test it yourself. Suppose amino acids are plentiful, so the Rags hold the complex right on the lysosome. Now remove the growth factor from outside the cell. Does the kinase switch on, or stay off?

scenes.visual: Hold the exact predict frame with slow ambient motion: cyan amino acid dots drift gently, gold mTORC1 stays docked on the lysosome, and a slim circular countdown ring fills quietly in the top-right corner over 4.5 seconds while the question banner remains visible.

scenes.tts: It stays off. Without the growth factor, AKT quiets down and the TSC brake returns to the lysosome. TSC drains Rheb of GTP, turning that activator off. Even sitting right beside Rheb, docked em-tor C one stays silent without an active partner.
scenes.caption: It stays off. Without the growth factor, Akt quiets down and the TSC brake returns to the lysosome. TSC drains Rheb of GTP, turning that activator off. Even sitting right beside Rheb, docked mTORC1 stays silent without an active partner.
scenes.visual: Question banner fades. Crimson 'TSC' glides back onto the lysosome rim and clamps onto Rheb; Rheb's emerald 'GTP' flips to dim grey 'GDP'. Gold 'mTORC1' stays docked on cyan Rags right beside dim Rheb, completely unlit, with a crisp label 'mTORC1 OFF' (size 30).
scenes.narration: It stays off. Without the growth factor, Akt quiets down and the TSC brake returns to the lysosome. TSC drains Rheb of GTP, turning that activator off. Even sitting right beside Rheb, docked mTORC1 stays silent without an active partner.

scenes.tts: Now restore the growth factor while amino acids remain plentiful. AKT clears the TSC brake, Rheb lights up with GTP, and docked em-tor C one fires. Once active, it speeds up protein building and lipid synthesis. At the same time, it holds off cellular self-digestion, called autophagy.
scenes.caption: Now restore the growth factor while amino acids remain plentiful. Akt clears the TSC brake, Rheb lights up with GTP, and docked mTORC1 fires. Once active, it speeds up protein building and lipid synthesis. At the same time, it holds off cellular self-digestion, called autophagy.
scenes.visual: Emerald growth factor returns; Akt glows; crimson TSC detaches; Rheb lights emerald 'Rheb-GTP'. Beside it, docked gold 'mTORC1' flares bright gold ('mTORC1 ON', size 30). Three crisp schematic outputs radiate outward: upward green arrows for 'Protein synthesis' and 'Lipid synthesis', and a crimson flat-headed bar blocking 'Autophagy' (all labels size 28, marked 'schematic').
scenes.narration: Now restore the growth factor while amino acids remain plentiful. Akt clears the TSC brake, Rheb lights up with GTP, and docked mTORC1 fires. Once active, it speeds up protein building and lipid synthesis. At the same time, it holds off cellular self-digestion, called autophagy.

scenes.tts: So em-tor C one needs both growth factors and amino acids to switch on. Growth factors activate Rheb, and amino acids deliver the kinase to meet it. This is the standard model, though some nutrients like glutamine can bypass the Rags. In normal cells, growth waits until both signals agree.
scenes.caption: So mTORC1 needs both growth factors and amino acids to switch on. Growth factors activate Rheb, and amino acids deliver the kinase to meet it. scenes.visual: Pull back smoothly to the whole cell schematic glowing in steady balance: emerald growth-factor track on the left ('Rheb ON'), sky-cyan amino-acid track on the right ('mTORC1 delivered'), converging at the lysosome ('AND gate', schematic). A brief side note reads 'Standard model (some Rag-independent routes)' before the scene gently dims to the end card.
scenes.narration: So mTORC1 needs both growth factors and amino acids to switch on. Growth factors activate Rheb, and amino acids deliver the kinase to meet it. This is the standard model, though some nutrients like glutamine can bypass the Rags. In normal cells, growth waits until both signals agree.
